title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — General Assessment #11

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #11
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Light.

2. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only carbon dioxide

3. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. joule (J)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. watt (W)

4. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Milk souring
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Paper burning to ash

5. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Overgrazing continuously

6. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 37 °C

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Properties of Matter? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Properties of Matter.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Properties of Matter.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Properties of Matter.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Matter.

8. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

9. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Heat? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Heat.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Heat.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Heat.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Heat.

11. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. Heating until a solid melts

12. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. A mixture of two liquids

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Heat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Matter and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.

2. A — Glucose and oxygen

3. A — newton (N)

4. C — Ice melting to water

5. C — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

6. B — 100 °C

7. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Matter.

8. D — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

9. B — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

10. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Heat.

11. C — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

12. A — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Water Conservation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Heat; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Properties of Matter; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
